title: Responsible AI
blurb: Fairness, transparency, explainability, safety and their measures.
source: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) exam guide · Domain 4
hint: Identify the source of harm and the matching control; documenting a risk, preventing it, detecting it, and requiring human approval are distinct safeguards.

items.label: Existing social or institutional inequality is reflected in the data used to build the system.
items.why: Existing social or institutional inequality is reflected in the data used to build the system.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.1 (responsible AI: sources of bias in datasets)

items.label: Some people, conditions, languages, or cases are underrepresented in the dataset.
items.why: Some people, conditions, languages, or cases are underrepresented in the dataset.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.1 (responsible AI: inclusivity and dataset representativeness)

items.label: The chosen feature or label is an imperfect and systematically distorted proxy for the real concept.
items.why: The chosen feature or label is an imperfect and systematically distorted proxy for the real concept.
items.citation: NIST SP 1270 (identifying and managing bias in AI: measurement and proxy bias)

items.label: Evaluates whether system quality and harms are acceptably distributed across relevant groups.
items.why: Evaluates whether system quality and harms are acceptably distributed across relevant groups.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.1 (responsible AI dimensions: fairness)

items.label: Helps people understand the factors or evidence contributing to a model output.
items.why: Helps people understand the factors or evidence contributing to a model output.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.2 (transparent and explainable models)

items.label: Communicates that AI is being used, its intended purpose, limitations, and accountable owner.
items.why: Communicates that AI is being used, its intended purpose, limitations, and accountable owner.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.2 (transparency: communicating AI use, purpose and limitations)

items.label: Places qualified people in review or approval paths for uncertain, sensitive, or consequential cases.
items.why: Places qualified people in review or approval paths for uncertain, sensitive, or consequential cases.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.1 (responsible AI: human oversight and safety)

items.label: Records where content came from and whether it was generated or modified by AI.
items.why: Records where content came from and whether it was generated or modified by AI.
items.citation: EU AI Act (transparency obligations: marking and provenance of AI-generated content)

items.label: Detects and removes personal data before it reaches a model, log, or unauthorized recipient.
items.why: Detects and removes personal data before it reaches a model, log, or unauthorized recipient.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 5.1 (securing AI systems: protecting personal data)

items.label: Gives a model, agent, or tool only the permissions required for its specific task.
items.why: Gives a model, agent, or tool only the permissions required for its specific task.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 5.1 (securing AI systems: IAM least-privilege access)

items.label: Untrusted instructions in user input or retrieved content attempt to redirect model behavior.
items.why: Untrusted instructions in user input or retrieved content attempt to redirect model behavior.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (prompt injection)

items.label: Malicious instructions hidden in external content are retrieved or read by an AI system.
items.why: Malicious instructions hidden in external content are retrieved or read by an AI system.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (indirect prompt injection via external content)

items.label: Input is crafted to evade behavioral safeguards and elicit prohibited output.
items.why: Input is crafted to evade behavioral safeguards and elicit prohibited output.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 3.2 (prompt engineering risks: jailbreaking)

items.label: Manipulated training examples introduce attacker-chosen behavior or systematic errors.
items.why: Manipulated training examples introduce attacker-chosen behavior or systematic errors.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (training data poisoning)

items.label: Malicious or misleading documents are inserted into a knowledge source to corrupt grounded answers.
items.why: Malicious or misleading documents are inserted into a knowledge source to corrupt grounded answers.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (poisoning of retrieval and embedding sources)

items.label: The system reveals confidential information through output, logs, memory, or tool results.
items.why: The system reveals confidential information through output, logs, memory, or tool results.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (sensitive information disclosure)

items.label: An agent can take consequential actions without adequate scope limits, confirmation, or supervision.
items.why: An agent can take consequential actions without adequate scope limits, confirmation, or supervision.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (excessive agency)

items.label: Abusive requests trigger excessive model or tool consumption and create avoidable cost.
items.why: Abusive requests trigger excessive model or tool consumption and create avoidable cost.
items.citation: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (unbounded consumption / denial of wallet)

items.label: Documents intended use, evaluation results, limitations, risks, and other facts about a model.
items.why: Documents intended use, evaluation results, limitations, risks, and other facts about a model.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 4.2 (transparency tools: model cards)

items.label: Records prompts, model versions, retrieved evidence, tool actions, approvals, and outcomes for accountability.
items.why: Records prompts, model versions, retrieved evidence, tool actions, approvals, and outcomes for accountability.
items.citation: AIF-C01 exam guide · Task 5.2 (governance: auditability and monitoring of AI systems)
